items.text:
अथातो हिमशैलाग्रे देवदारुवनालये ।
व्यासं एकाग्रं आसीनं अपृच्छन्नृषयः पुरा ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
athāto himaśailāgre devadāruvanālaye |
vyāsaṃ ekāgraṃ āsīnaṃ apṛcchannṛṣayaḥ purā || 1 ||
items.en: Long ago, on a peak of the Himalaya, in a forest of deodar trees, the sages questioned Vyāsa as he sat with a focused mind.

items.text:
मानुषाणां हितं धर्मं वर्तमाने कलौ युगे ।
शौचाचारं यथावच्च वद सत्यवतीसुत ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
mānuṣāṇāṃ hitaṃ dharmaṃ vartamāne kalau yuge |
śaucācāraṃ yathāvacca vada satyavatīsuta || 2 ||
items.en: 'Son of Satyavatī, tell us the dharma that is good for human beings in the present Kali age, and the proper rules of purity and conduct.'
items.note: Kali age (Kali yuga): the last and most degenerate of the four world ages, believed to be the present one.

items.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा ऋषिवाक्यं तु सशिष्योऽग्न्यर्कसंनिभः ।
प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः श्रुतिस्मृतिविशारदः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
tacchrutvā ṛṣivākyaṃ tu saśiṣyo'gnyarkasaṃnibhaḥ |
pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ śrutismṛtiviśāradaḥ || 3 ||
items.en: Hearing the sages' words, the greatly radiant Vyāsa, bright as fire and the sun, expert in Śruti and Smṛti, surrounded by his disciples, replied:
items.note: Śruti: the revealed Veda. Smṛti: the remembered law books, such as this one.

items.text:
न चाहं सर्वतत्त्वज्ञः कथं धर्मं वदाम्यहम् ।
अस्मत्पितैव प्रष्टव्य इति व्यासः सुतोऽब्रवीत् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
na cāhaṃ sarvatattvajñaḥ kathaṃ dharmaṃ vadāmyaham |
asmatpitaiva praṣṭavya iti vyāsaḥ suto'bravīt || 4 ||
items.en: 'I do not know the full truth of everything, so how can I teach dharma? My own father should be asked,' said Vyāsa, the son (of Parāśara).

items.text:
ततस्त ऋषयः सर्वे धर्मतत्त्वार्थकाङ्क्षिणः ।
ऋषिं व्यासं पुरस्कृत्य गता बदरिकाश्रमं ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
tatasta ṛṣayaḥ sarve dharmatattvārthakāṅkṣiṇaḥ |
ṛṣiṃ vyāsaṃ puraskṛtya gatā badarikāśramaṃ || 5 ||
items.en: Then all those sages, eager to learn the true meaning of dharma, went to the hermitage of Badarī, with the sage Vyāsa at their head.

items.text:
नानापुष्पलताकीर्णं फलवृष्कैरलंकृतम् ।
नदीप्रस्रवणोपेतं पुण्यतीर्थोपशोभितं ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
nānāpuṣpalatākīrṇaṃ phalavṛṣkairalaṃkṛtam |
nadīprasravaṇopetaṃ puṇyatīrthopaśobhitaṃ || 6 ||
items.en: That hermitage was full of many kinds of flowers and creepers, adorned with fruit trees, with rivers and springs, and graced by holy bathing places.

items.text:
मृगपक्षिनिनादाढ्यं देवतायतनावृतम् ।
यक्षगन्धर्वसिद्धैश्च नृत्यगीतैरलंकृतम् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
mṛgapakṣininādāḍhyaṃ devatāyatanāvṛtam |
yakṣagandharvasiddhaiśca nṛtyagītairalaṃkṛtam || 7 ||
items.en: It was filled with the cries of animals and birds, surrounded by temples, and made beautiful by the dancing and singing of Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Siddhas.
items.note: Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Siddhas: kinds of semi-divine beings.

items.text:
तस्मिन्नृषिसभामध्ये शक्तिपुत्रं पराशरम् ।
सुखासीनं महातेजा मुनिमुख्यगणावृतं ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
tasminnṛṣisabhāmadhye śaktiputraṃ parāśaram |
sukhāsīnaṃ mahātejā munimukhyagaṇāvṛtaṃ || 8 ||
items.en: There, in the middle of the assembly of sages, sat Parāśara, the son of Śakti, at ease and full of radiance, surrounded by groups of the chief sages.

items.text:
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा व्यासस्तु ऋषिभिः सह ।
प्रदक्षिणाभिवादैश्च स्तुतिभिः समपूजयत् ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā vyāsastu ṛṣibhiḥ saha |
pradakṣiṇābhivādaiśca stutibhiḥ samapūjayat || 9 ||
items.en: Vyāsa, together with the sages, joined his palms in respect and honoured him by walking around him, bowing to him, and praising him.

items.text:
ततः संतुष्टहृदयः पराशरमहामुनिः ।
आह सुस्वागतं ब्रूहीत्यासीनो मुनिपुङ्गवः ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ saṃtuṣṭahṛdayaḥ parāśaramahāmuniḥ |
āha susvāgataṃ brūhītyāsīno munipuṅgavaḥ || 10 ||
items.en: Then the great sage Parāśara, pleased at heart, remained seated and said: 'You are welcome. Speak.'

items.text:
कुशलं सम्यगित्युक्त्वा व्यासः पृच्छत्यनन्तरम् ।
यदि जानासि भक्तिं मे स्नेहाद्वा भक्तवत्सल ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
kuśalaṃ samyagityuktvā vyāsaḥ pṛcchatyanantaram |
yadi jānāsi bhaktiṃ me snehādvā bhaktavatsala || 11 ||
items.en: Vyāsa said, 'All is well,' and then asked: 'You who are kind to your devotees, if you know my devotion to you, or out of affection,

items.text:
धर्मं कथय मे तात अनुग्राह्यो ह्यहं तव ।
श्रुता मे मानवा धर्मा वासिष्ठा काश्यपास्तथा ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
dharmaṃ kathaya me tāta anugrāhyo hyahaṃ tava |
śrutā me mānavā dharmā vāsiṣṭhā kāśyapāstathā || 12 ||
items.en: … teach me dharma, dear father, for I deserve your kindness. I have heard the laws of Manu, of Vasiṣṭha and of Kaśyapa,

items.text:
गर्गेया गौतमीयाश्च तथा चोशनसा स्मृताः ।
अत्रेर्विष्णोश्च संवर्ताद्दक्षादङ्गिरसस्तथा ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
gargeyā gautamīyāśca tathā cośanasā smṛtāḥ |
atrerviṣṇośca saṃvartāddakṣādaṅgirasastathā || 13 ||
items.en: … and those of Garga and Gautama, and the laws of Uśanas; and those from Atri, Viṣṇu, Saṃvarta, Dakṣa and Aṅgiras,

items.text:
शातातपाच्च हारीताद्याज्ञवल्क्यात्तथैव च ।
आपस्तम्बकृता धर्मा शङ्खस्य लिखितस्य च ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
śātātapācca hārītādyājñavalkyāttathaiva ca |
āpastambakṛtā dharmā śaṅkhasya likhitasya ca || 14 ||
items.en: … from Śātātapa, Hārīta and Yājñavalkya; the laws made by Āpastamba, and those of Śaṅkha and Likhita,

items.text:
कात्यायनकृताश्चैव तथा प्राचेतसान्मुनेः ।
श्रुता ह्येते भवत्प्रोक्ताः श्रुत्यर्था मे न विस्मृताः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
kātyāyanakṛtāścaiva tathā prācetasānmuneḥ |
śrutā hyete bhavatproktāḥ śrutyarthā me na vismṛtāḥ || 15 ||
items.en: … and those made by Kātyāyana and by the sage Prācetasa. I have heard all these as you explained them, and I have not forgotten the meaning of the Veda.

items.text:
अस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे धर्माः कृतत्रेतादिके युगे ।
सर्वे धर्माः कृते जाताः सर्वे नष्टाः कलौ युगे ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
asminmanvantare dharmāḥ kṛtatretādike yuge |
sarve dharmāḥ kṛte jātāḥ sarve naṣṭāḥ kalau yuge || 16 ||
items.en: 'In this Manvantara the dharmas belong to the ages beginning with Kṛta and Tretā. All dharmas arose in the Kṛta age, and all are lost in the Kali age.
items.note: Manvantara: the long period ruled by one Manu. Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, Kali: the four world ages, each worse than the one before.

items.text:
चातुर्वर्ण्यसमाचारं किंचित्साधारणं वद ।
चतुर्णां अपि वर्णानां कर्तव्यं धर्मकोविदैः ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
cāturvarṇyasamācāraṃ kiṃcitsādhāraṇaṃ vada |
caturṇāṃ api varṇānāṃ kartavyaṃ dharmakovidaiḥ || 17 ||
items.en: Tell me something of the conduct of the four varṇas that is common to all, which those who know dharma must follow for all four varṇas.
items.note: varṇa: one of the four social classes (brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, śūdra).

items.text:
ब्रूहि धर्मस्वरूपज्ञ सूक्ष्मं स्थूलं च विस्तरात् ।
व्यासवाक्यावसाने तु मुनिमुख्यः पराशरः ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
brūhi dharmasvarūpajña sūkṣmaṃ sthūlaṃ ca vistarāt |
vyāsavākyāvasāne tu munimukhyaḥ parāśaraḥ || 18 ||
items.en: You who know the nature of dharma, explain it in detail, both its fine points and its broad rules.' When Vyāsa had finished speaking, Parāśara, chief of sages,

items.text:
धर्मस्य निर्णयं प्राह सूक्ष्मं स्थूलं च विस्तरात् ।
शृणु पुत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि शृण्वन्तु मुनयस्तथा ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
dharmasya nirṇayaṃ prāha sūkṣmaṃ sthūlaṃ ca vistarāt |
śṛṇu putra pravakṣyāmi śṛṇvantu munayastathā || 19 ||
items.en: … explained the settled rules of dharma in detail, both the fine points and the broad ones: 'Listen, son, I will explain; and let the sages listen too.

items.text:
कल्पे कल्पे क्षयोत्पत्त्या ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ।
श्रुतिस्मृतिसदाचार निर्णेतारश्च सर्वदा ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
kalpe kalpe kṣayotpattyā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ |
śrutismṛtisadācāra nirṇetāraśca sarvadā || 20 ||
items.en: In every kalpa, as the world is destroyed and created again, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara (Śiva) are always the ones who settle Śruti, Smṛti and good custom.
items.note: kalpa: a vast cosmic cycle, one 'day' of Brahmā.

items.text:
न कश्चिद्वेदकर्ता च वेदं स्मृत्वा चतुर्मुखः ।
तथैव धर्मान्स्मरति मनुः कल्पान्तरेऽन्तरे ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
na kaścidvedakartā ca vedaṃ smṛtvā caturmukhaḥ |
tathaiva dharmānsmarati manuḥ kalpāntare'ntare || 21 ||
items.en: No one is the author of the Veda. Four-faced Brahmā remembers the Veda, and in the same way Manu remembers the dharmas in each new kalpa.

items.text:
अन्ये कृतयुगे धर्मास्त्रेतायां द्वापरे युगे ।
अन्ये कलियुगे नॄणां युगरूपानुसारतः ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
anye kṛtayuge dharmāstretāyāṃ dvāpare yuge |
anye kaliyuge nṝṇāṃ yugarūpānusārataḥ || 22 ||
items.en: The dharmas of people in the Kṛta age are different, those in Tretā and Dvāpara are different, and those in the Kali age are different again, according to the nature of each age.

items.text:
तपः परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां ज्ञानं उच्यते ।
द्वापरे यज्ञं एवाहुः दानं एव कलौ युगे ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
tapaḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ jñānaṃ ucyate |
dvāpare yajñaṃ evāhuḥ dānaṃ eva kalau yuge || 23 ||
items.en: In the Kṛta age austerity is highest; in Tretā, knowledge; in Dvāpara, sacrifice; and in the Kali age, only giving.

items.text:
कृते तु मानवा धर्मास्त्रेतायां गौतमाः स्मृताः ।
द्वापरे शाङ्खलिखिताः कलौ पाराशराः स्मृताः ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
kṛte tu mānavā dharmāstretāyāṃ gautamāḥ smṛtāḥ |
dvāpare śāṅkhalikhitāḥ kalau pārāśarāḥ smṛtāḥ || 24 ||
items.en: In the Kṛta age the laws of Manu apply; in Tretā, those of Gautama; in Dvāpara, those of Śaṅkha and Likhita; and in the Kali age, those of Parāśara.

items.text:
त्यजेद्देशं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां ग्रामं उत्सृजेत् ।
द्वापरे कुलं एकं तु कर्तारं तु कलौ युगे ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
tyajeddeśaṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ grāmaṃ utsṛjet |
dvāpare kulaṃ ekaṃ tu kartāraṃ tu kalau yuge || 25 ||
items.en: (To avoid a sinner,) in the Kṛta age one should leave the whole country; in Tretā, leave the village; in Dvāpara, only his family; and in the Kali age, only the doer himself.

items.text:
कृते संभाषणादेव त्रेतायां स्पर्शनेन च ।
द्वापरे त्वन्नं आदाय कलौ पतति कर्मणा ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
kṛte saṃbhāṣaṇādeva tretāyāṃ sparśanena ca |
dvāpare tvannaṃ ādāya kalau patati karmaṇā || 26 ||
items.en: In the Kṛta age a man falls (from his caste) just by talking (with a fallen person); in Tretā, by touching him; in Dvāpara, by taking his food; in the Kali age, only by his own act.

items.text:
कृते तात्कालिकः शापस्त्रेतायां दशभिर्दिनैः ।
द्वापरे चैकमासेन कलौ संवत्सरेण तु ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
kṛte tātkālikaḥ śāpastretāyāṃ daśabhirdinaiḥ |
dvāpare caikamāsena kalau saṃvatsareṇa tu || 27 ||
items.en: In the Kṛta age a curse takes effect at once; in Tretā, in ten days; in Dvāpara, in one month; and in the Kali age, in one year.

items.text:
अभिगम्य कृते दानं त्रेतास्वाहूय दीयते ।
द्वापरे याचमानाय सेवया दीयते कलौ ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
abhigamya kṛte dānaṃ tretāsvāhūya dīyate |
dvāpare yācamānāya sevayā dīyate kalau || 28 ||
items.en: In the Kṛta age a gift is given by going to the receiver; in Tretā, by calling him; in Dvāpara, to one who asks; and in the Kali age, in return for service.

items.text:
अभिगम्योत्तमं दानं आहूयैव तु मध्यमम् ।
अधमं याचमानाय सेवादानं तु निष्फलं ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
abhigamyottamaṃ dānaṃ āhūyaiva tu madhyamam |
adhamaṃ yācamānāya sevādānaṃ tu niṣphalaṃ || 29 ||
items.en: A gift given by going to the receiver is the best; one given after calling him is middling; one given to a person who asks is the lowest; and a gift given for service bears no fruit.

items.text:
जितो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं चैवानृतेन च ।
जिताश्चोरैश्च राजानः स्त्रीभिश्च पुरुषाः कलौ ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
jito dharmo hyadharmeṇa satyaṃ caivānṛtena ca |
jitāścoraiśca rājānaḥ strībhiśca puruṣāḥ kalau || 30 ||
items.en: In the Kali age, dharma is defeated by adharma, truth by falsehood, kings by thieves, and men by women.

items.text:
सीदन्ति चाग्निहोत्राणि गुरुपूजा प्रणश्यति ।
कुमार्यश्च प्रसूयन्ते अस्मिन्कलियुगे सदा ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
sīdanti cāgnihotrāṇi gurupūjā praṇaśyati |
kumāryaśca prasūyante asminkaliyuge sadā || 31 ||
items.en: In this Kali age the agnihotra fires decline, respect for teachers disappears, and unmarried girls always give birth.
items.note: agnihotra: the daily fire offering kept by a householder.

items.text:
कृते त्वस्थिगताः प्राणास्त्रेतायां मांसं आश्रिताः ।
द्वापरे रुधिरं चैव कलौ त्वन्नादिषु स्थिताः ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
kṛte tvasthigatāḥ prāṇāstretāyāṃ māṃsaṃ āśritāḥ |
dvāpare rudhiraṃ caiva kalau tvannādiṣu sthitāḥ || 32 ||
items.en: In the Kṛta age life rests in the bones; in Tretā, in the flesh; in Dvāpara, in the blood; and in the Kali age it depends on food and the like.

items.text:
युगे युगे च ये धर्मास्तत्र तत्र च ये द्विजाः ।
तेषां निन्दा न कर्तव्या युगरूपा हि ते द्विजाः ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
yuge yuge ca ye dharmāstatra tatra ca ye dvijāḥ |
teṣāṃ nindā na kartavyā yugarūpā hi te dvijāḥ || 33 ||
items.en: The dharmas of each age, and the twice-born of each age, should not be blamed, for those twice-born are shaped by their age.
items.note: twice-born (dvija): men of the brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya and vaiśya classes, who receive the sacred thread.

items.text:
युगे युगे तु सामर्थ्यं शेषं मुनिविभाषितम् ।
पराशरेण चाप्युक्तं प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
yuge yuge tu sāmarthyaṃ śeṣaṃ munivibhāṣitam |
parāśareṇa cāpyuktaṃ prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate || 34 ||
items.en: In each age people have their own strength. The rest has been taught by the sages, and now the prāyaścitta taught by Parāśara is laid down.
items.note: prāyaścitta: an act of expiation or penance that removes sin. The first half-line is terse; the reading is approximate.

items.text:
अहं अद्यैव तत्सर्वं अनुस्मृत्य ब्रवीमि वः ।
चातुर्वर्ण्यसमाचारं शृण्वन्तु ऋषिपुङ्गवाः ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
ahaṃ adyaiva tatsarvaṃ anusmṛtya bravīmi vaḥ |
cāturvarṇyasamācāraṃ śṛṇvantu ṛṣipuṅgavāḥ || 35 ||
items.en: Today I will recall all of it and tell you. Let the chief sages listen to the rules of conduct for the four varṇas.

items.text:
पराशरमतं पुण्यं पवित्रं पापनाशनम् ।
चिन्तितं ब्राह्मणार्थाय धर्मसंस्थापनाय च ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
parāśaramataṃ puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam |
cintitaṃ brāhmaṇārthāya dharmasaṃsthāpanāya ca || 36 ||
items.en: The teaching of Parāśara is holy, purifying and destroys sin. It was thought out for the good of brāhmaṇas and to establish dharma.

items.text:
चतुर्णां अपि वर्णानां आचारो धर्मपालकः ।
आचारभ्रष्टदेहानां भवेद्धर्मः पराङ्मुखः ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
caturṇāṃ api varṇānāṃ ācāro dharmapālakaḥ |
ācārabhraṣṭadehānāṃ bhaveddharmaḥ parāṅmukhaḥ || 37 ||
items.en: For all four varṇas, right conduct is what protects dharma. For those who have fallen from right conduct, dharma turns its face away.

items.text:
षट्कर्माभिरतो नित्यं देवतातिथिपूजकः ।
हुतशेषं तु भुञ्जानो ब्राह्मणो नावसीदति ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
ṣaṭkarmābhirato nityaṃ devatātithipūjakaḥ |
hutaśeṣaṃ tu bhuñjāno brāhmaṇo nāvasīdati || 38 ||
items.en: A brāhmaṇa who is always devoted to the six duties, honours gods and guests, and eats what is left after the offering, does not come to ruin.

items.text:
संध्यास्नानं जपो होमो देवतातिथिपूजनम् ।
आतिथ्यं वैश्वदेवं च षट्कर्माणि दिने दिने ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
saṃdhyāsnānaṃ japo homo devatātithipūjanam |
ātithyaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca ṣaṭkarmāṇi dine dine || 39 ||
items.en: The six duties to be done every day are: bathing with the saṃdhyā prayer, japa, homa, worship of the gods, hospitality to guests, and the vaiśvadeva offering.
items.note: saṃdhyā: prayers at dawn, noon and dusk. japa: quiet repetition of a mantra. homa: offering into the sacred fire. vaiśvadeva: a daily food offering to all the gods before the meal.

items.text:
इष्टो वा यदि वा द्वेष्यो मूर्खः पण्डित एव वा ।
संप्राप्तो वैश्वदेवान्ते सोऽतिथिः स्वर्गसंग्रमः ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
iṣṭo vā yadi vā dveṣyo mūrkhaḥ paṇḍita eva vā |
saṃprāpto vaiśvadevānte so'tithiḥ svargasaṃgramaḥ || 40 ||
items.en: Whether liked or disliked, a fool or a learned man, whoever arrives at the end of the vaiśvadeva offering is a guest and a way to heaven.

items.text:
दूराध्वोपगतं श्रान्तं वैश्वदेव उपस्थितम् ।
अतिथिं तं विजानीयान्नातिथिः पूर्वं आगतः ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr:
dūrādhvopagataṃ śrāntaṃ vaiśvadeva upasthitam |
atithiṃ taṃ vijānīyānnātithiḥ pūrvaṃ āgataḥ || 41 ||
items.en: Know as a guest the one who has come from far away, is tired, and arrives at the time of the vaiśvadeva. One who has come before is not a guest.

items.text:
नैकग्रामीणं अतिथिं संगृह्णीत कदाचन ।
अनित्यं आगतो यस्मात्तस्मादतिथिरुच्यते ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr:
naikagrāmīṇaṃ atithiṃ saṃgṛhṇīta kadācana |
anityaṃ āgato yasmāttasmādatithirucyate || 42 ||
items.en: Never receive a man of the same village as a guest. He is called atithi (guest) because he comes at no fixed time (anitya).
items.note: A word play: atithi 'guest' is linked to 'one who does not stay (a fixed) day'.

items.text:
अतिथिं तत्र संप्राप्तं पूजयेत्स्वागतादिना ।
अर्घ्यासनप्रदानेन पादप्रक्षालनेन च ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr:
atithiṃ tatra saṃprāptaṃ pūjayetsvāgatādinā |
arghyāsanapradānena pādaprakṣālanena ca || 43 ||
items.en: When a guest arrives, honour him with words of welcome, by offering water and a seat, and by washing his feet,

items.text:
श्रद्धया चान्नदानेन प्रियप्रश्नोत्तरेण च ।
गच्छन्तं चानुयानेन प्रीतिं उत्पादयेद्गृही ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr:
śraddhayā cānnadānena priyapraśnottareṇa ca |
gacchantaṃ cānuyānena prītiṃ utpādayedgṛhī || 44 ||
items.en: … with food given with respect, with kind questions and answers, and by walking with him a little when he leaves. In this way the householder should make him happy.

items.text:
अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशो गृहात्प्रतिनिवर्तते ।
पितरस्तस्य नाश्नन्ति दश वर्षाणि पञ्च च ॥ ४५ ॥
items.tr:
atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhātpratinivartate |
pitarastasya nāśnanti daśa varṣāṇi pañca ca || 45 ||
items.en: If a guest leaves a man's house with his hopes broken, that man's ancestors do not eat (his offerings) for fifteen years.

items.text:
काष्ठभारसहस्रेण घृतकुम्भशतेन च ।
अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशस्तस्य होमो निरर्थकः ॥ ४६ ॥
items.tr:
kāṣṭhabhārasahasreṇa ghṛtakumbhaśatena ca |
atithiryasya bhagnāśastasya homo nirarthakaḥ || 46 ||
items.en: Even with a thousand loads of firewood and a hundred pots of ghee, the fire offering of a man who disappoints a guest is useless.

items.text:
सुक्षेत्रे वापयेद्बीजं सुपात्रे निक्षिपेद्धनम् ।
सुक्षेत्रे च सुपात्रे च ह्युप्तं दत्तं न नश्यति ॥ ४७ ॥
items.tr:
sukṣetre vāpayedbījaṃ supātre nikṣipeddhanam |
sukṣetre ca supātre ca hyuptaṃ dattaṃ na naśyati || 47 ||
items.en: One should sow seed in good soil and place wealth with a worthy person. What is sown in good soil and given to a worthy person is never lost.

items.text:
न पृच्छेद्गोत्रचरणे न स्वाध्यायं श्रुतं तथा ।
हृदये कल्पयेद्देवं सर्वदेवमयो हि सः ॥ ४८ ॥
items.tr:
na pṛcchedgotracaraṇe na svādhyāyaṃ śrutaṃ tathā |
hṛdaye kalpayeddevaṃ sarvadevamayo hi saḥ || 48 ||
items.en: Do not ask the guest about his gotra or Vedic school, nor about his study or learning. Think of him in your heart as a god, for he contains all the gods.
items.note: gotra: a clan or family line traced to an ancient sage.

items.text:
अपूर्वः सुव्रती विप्रो ह्यपूर्वश्चातितिहिर्यथा ।
वेदाभ्यासरतो नित्यं तावपूर्वौ दिने दिने ॥ ४९ ॥
items.tr:
apūrvaḥ suvratī vipro hyapūrvaścātitihiryathā |
vedābhyāsarato nityaṃ tāvapūrvau dine dine || 49 ||
items.en: A brāhmaṇa of good vows, always devoted to Vedic study, is something rare, and so is a guest; these two are rare every day.
items.note: Meaning unclear: 'apūrva' may mean 'rare' or 'bringing unseen merit'. Best reading given.

items.text:
वैश्वदेवे तु संप्राप्ते भिक्षुके गृहं आगते ।
उद्धृत्य वैश्वदेवार्थं भिक्षुकं तु विसर्जयेत् ॥ ५० ॥
items.tr:
vaiśvadeve tu saṃprāpte bhikṣuke gṛhaṃ āgate |
uddhṛtya vaiśvadevārthaṃ bhikṣukaṃ tu visarjayet || 50 ||
items.en: If a beggar comes to the house when it is time for the vaiśvadeva, one should set aside the portion for the vaiśvadeva, (give him alms,) and send the beggar away.

items.text:
यतिश्च ब्रह्मचारी च पक्वान्नस्वामिनावुभौ ।
तयोरन्नं अदत्त्वा तु भुक्त्वा चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ॥ ५१ ॥
items.tr:
yatiśca brahmacārī ca pakvānnasvāmināvubhau |
tayorannaṃ adattvā tu bhuktvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret || 51 ||
items.en: A yati and a brahmacārī are both owners of cooked food. Whoever eats without giving them food must perform the Cāndrāyaṇa.
items.note: yati: a renouncer, wandering ascetic. brahmacārī: a celibate Vedic student. Cāndrāyaṇa: a month-long penance in which daily food is cut down and increased with the phases of the moon.

items.text:
दद्याच्च भिक्षात्रितयं परिव्राड्ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ।
इच्छया च ततो दद्याद्विभवे सत्यवारितं ॥ ५२ ॥
items.tr:
dadyācca bhikṣātritayaṃ parivrāḍbrahmacāriṇām |
icchayā ca tato dadyādvibhave satyavāritaṃ || 52 ||
items.en: One should give three portions of alms to wandering ascetics and students; after that, if one has the means, one may give more as one wishes, without limit.

items.text:
यतिहस्ते जलं दद्याद्भैक्षं दद्यात्पुनर्जलम् ।
तद्भैक्ष्यं मेरुणा तुल्यं तज्जलं सागरोपमम् ॥ ५३ ॥
items.tr:
yatihaste jalaṃ dadyādbhaikṣaṃ dadyātpunarjalam |
tadbhaikṣyaṃ meruṇā tulyaṃ tajjalaṃ sāgaropamam || 53 ||
items.en: Put water in the ascetic's hand, then give the alms, then water again. Those alms become equal to Mount Meru, and that water like the ocean.

items.text:
यस्य छत्रं हयश्चैव कुञ्जरारोहं ऋद्धिमत् ।
ऐन्द्रं स्थानं उपासीत तस्मात्तं न विचारयेत् ॥ ५४ ॥
items.tr:
yasya chatraṃ hayaścaiva kuñjarārohaṃ ṛddhimat |
aindraṃ sthānaṃ upāsīta tasmāttaṃ na vicārayet || 54 ||
items.en: One who has a royal umbrella, horses, elephants to ride and great wealth would come to the place of Indra; therefore one should not question (the guest).
items.note: Unclear verse; the link between the two halves is uncertain. Best reading given.

items.text:
वैश्वदेवकृतं पापं शक्तो भिक्षुर्व्यपोहितुम् ।
न हि भिक्षुकृतान्दोषान्वैश्वदेवो व्यपोहति ॥ ५५ ॥
items.tr:
vaiśvadevakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ śakto bhikṣurvyapohitum |
na hi bhikṣukṛtāndoṣānvaiśvadevo vyapohati || 55 ||
items.en: A beggar can remove a sin made in the vaiśvadeva, but the vaiśvadeva cannot remove the faults made against a beggar.

items.text:
अकृत्वा वैश्वदेवं तु भुञ्जते ये द्विजाधमाः ।
सर्वे ते निष्फला ज्ञेयाः पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥ ५६ ॥
items.tr:
akṛtvā vaiśvadevaṃ tu bhuñjate ye dvijādhamāḥ |
sarve te niṣphalā jñeyāḥ patanti narake'śucau || 56 ||
items.en: Those low twice-born men who eat without doing the vaiśvadeva: know that all of them are fruitless, and they fall into a filthy hell.

items.text:
वैश्वदेवविहीना ये आतिथ्येन बहिष्कृताः ।
सर्वे ते नरकं यान्ति काकयोनिं व्रजन्ति च ॥ ५७ ॥
items.tr:
vaiśvadevavihīnā ye ātithyena bahiṣkṛtāḥ |
sarve te narakaṃ yānti kākayoniṃ vrajanti ca || 57 ||
items.en: Those who lack the vaiśvadeva and have given up hospitality all go to hell and are born as crows.

items.text:
पापो वा यदि चण्डालो विप्रघ्नः पितृघातकः ।
वैश्वदेवे तु संप्राप्तः सोऽतिथिः स्वर्गसंक्रमः ॥ ५८ ॥
items.tr:
pāpo vā yadi caṇḍālo vipraghnaḥ pitṛghātakaḥ |
vaiśvadeve tu saṃprāptaḥ so'tithiḥ svargasaṃkramaḥ || 58 ||
items.en: Even a sinner, a caṇḍāla, a killer of a brāhmaṇa or a killer of his father, if he arrives at the time of the vaiśvadeva, is a guest and a way to heaven.
items.note: caṇḍāla: a man of the lowest outcaste group.

items.text:
यो वेष्टितशिरा भुङ्क्ते यो भुङ्क्ते दक्षिणामुखः ।
वामपादे करं न्यस्य तद्वै रक्षांसि भुञ्जते ॥ ५९ ॥
items.tr:
yo veṣṭitaśirā bhuṅkte yo bhuṅkte dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ |
vāmapāde karaṃ nyasya tadvai rakṣāṃsi bhuñjate || 59 ||
items.en: If a man eats with his head covered, or eats facing south, or eats with his hand resting on his left foot, then demons eat that food.

items.text:
अव्रता ह्यनधीयाना यत्र भैक्षचरा द्विजाः ।
तं ग्रामं दण्डयेद्राजा चोरभक्तप्रदो हि सः ॥ ६० ॥
items.tr:
avratā hyanadhīyānā yatra bhaikṣacarā dvijāḥ |
taṃ grāmaṃ daṇḍayedrājā corabhaktaprado hi saḥ || 60 ||
items.en: Where twice-born men who keep no vows and do not study live by begging, the king should punish that village, for it feeds thieves.

items.text:
क्षत्रियो हि प्रजा रक्षञ् शस्त्रपाणिः प्रदण्डवान् ।
निर्जित्य परसैन्यानि क्षितिं धर्मेण पालयेत् ॥ ६१ ॥
items.tr:
kṣatriyo hi prajā rakṣañ śastrapāṇiḥ pradaṇḍavān |
nirjitya parasainyāni kṣitiṃ dharmeṇa pālayet || 61 ||
items.en: A kṣatriya, weapon in hand, protecting the people and punishing wrongdoers, should defeat enemy armies and rule the earth by dharma.

items.text:
पुष्पं पुष्पं विचिनुयान्मूलच्छेदं न कारयेत् ।
मालाकार इवारामे न यथाङ्गारकारकः ॥ ६२ ॥
items.tr:
puṣpaṃ puṣpaṃ vicinuyānmūlacchedaṃ na kārayet |
mālākāra ivārāme na yathāṅgārakārakaḥ || 62 ||
items.en: (In taking taxes) he should pick flower by flower and not cut the root, like a gardener in a garden, not like a charcoal-maker.

items.text:
लाभकर्म तथा रत्नं गवां च परिपालनम् ।
कृषिकर्म च वाणिज्यं वैश्यवृत्तिरुदाहृता ॥ ६३ ॥
items.tr:
lābhakarma tathā ratnaṃ gavāṃ ca paripālanam |
kṛṣikarma ca vāṇijyaṃ vaiśyavṛttirudāhṛtā || 63 ||
items.en: Lending for profit, dealing in gems, tending cattle, farming and trade are said to be the livelihood of a vaiśya.

items.text:
शूद्रस्य द्विजशुश्रूषा परमो धर्म उच्यते ।
अन्यथा कुरुते किंचित्तद्भवेत्तस्य निष्फलं ॥ ६४ ॥
items.tr:
śūdrasya dvijaśuśrūṣā paramo dharma ucyate |
anyathā kurute kiṃcittadbhavettasya niṣphalaṃ || 64 ||
items.en: Service to the twice-born is said to be the highest dharma of a śūdra. Whatever else he does bears no fruit for him.

items.text:
लवणं मधुतैलं च दधितक्रं घृतं पयः ।
न दुष्येच्छूद्रजातीनां कुर्यात्सर्वेषु विक्रयं ॥ ६५ ॥
items.tr:
lavaṇaṃ madhutailaṃ ca dadhitakraṃ ghṛtaṃ payaḥ |
na duṣyecchūdrajātīnāṃ kuryātsarveṣu vikrayaṃ || 65 ||
items.en: Salt, honey, oil, curd, buttermilk, ghee and milk are not made impure by śūdras; they may sell all of these.

items.text:
विक्रीणन्मध्यमांसानि ह्यभक्षस्य च भक्षणम् ।
कुर्वन्नगम्या गमनं शूद्रः पतति तत्क्षणात् ॥ ६६ ॥
items.tr:
vikrīṇanmadhyamāṃsāni hyabhakṣasya ca bhakṣaṇam |
kurvannagamyā gamanaṃ śūdraḥ patati tatkṣaṇāt || 66 ||
items.en: A śūdra who sells liquor and meat, eats forbidden food, or goes to a woman forbidden to him falls (from his caste) at once.

items.text:
कपिलाक्षीरपानेन ब्राह्मणीगमनेन च ।
वेदाक्षरविचारेण शूद्रश्चाण्डालतां व्रजेत् ॥ ६७ ॥
items.tr:
kapilākṣīrapānena brāhmaṇīgamanena ca |
vedākṣaravicāreṇa śūdraścāṇḍālatāṃ vrajet || 67 ||
items.en: By drinking the milk of a brown (kapilā) cow, by going to a brāhmaṇa woman, and by studying the syllables of the Veda, a śūdra becomes a caṇḍāla.
